\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{மின்வெட்டு} (miṉveṭṭu)}{மின்வெட்டு (miṉveṭṭu)}]{\ta{மின்வெட்டு} (miṉveṭṭu) — a power cut}

\label{lesson:TA-C445-minvettu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a stain, then the Tamil for to drip.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{மின்வெட்டு}}
\textbf{\ta{மின்வெட்டு}} — \emph{miṉveṭṭu} — \textquotedblleft{}a power cut\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{நேற்று} \ta{இரவு} \ta{மூன்று} \ta{மணி} \ta{நேரம்} \ta{மின்வெட்டு} \ta{இருந்தது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nēṟṟu iravu mūṉṟu maṇi nēram miṉveṭṭu iruntatu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Last night there was a power cut for three hours.
\end{quote}

\ta{மின்}, electricity, + \ta{வெட்டு}, a cut.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{மின்வெட்டு}} (\emph{miṉveṭṭu}) is built from \ta{மின்}, \textquotedblleft{}lightning, electricity\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 4876), and \ta{வெட்டு}, \textquotedblleft{}to cut; a cut\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 5478).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{miṉveṭṭu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{miṉveṭṭu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nēṟṟu iravu mūṉṟu maṇi nēram miṉveṭṭu iruntatu.} — Last night there was a power cut for three hours.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a stain, then the Tamil for to drip, then say \emph{miṉveṭṭu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{மின்வெட்டு} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A power cut\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{பஞ்சம்} (pañcam)}{பஞ்சம் (pañcam)}]{\ta{பஞ்சம்} (pañcam) — a scarcity; a famine}

\label{lesson:TA-C445-pancam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to drip, then the Tamil for a power cut.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{பஞ்சம்}}
\textbf{\ta{பஞ்சம்}} — \emph{pañcam} — \textquotedblleft{}a scarcity; a famine\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{கோடையில்} \ta{ஊரில்} \ta{தண்ணீர்ப்} \ta{பஞ்சம்} \ta{வந்தது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kōṭaiyil ūril taṇṇīrp pañcam vantatu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In summer the town ran short of water.
\end{quote}

\ta{தண்ணீர்ப்} \ta{பஞ்சம்} is a water shortage.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{பஞ்சம்}} (\emph{pañcam}) is native Dravidian (DEDR 3825), \textquotedblleft{}scarcity, famine\textquotedblright{}; the same article holds \ta{பசி}, \textquotedblleft{}hunger\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pañcam}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pañcam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kōṭaiyil ūril taṇṇīrp pañcam vantatu.} — In summer the town ran short of water.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to drip, then the Tamil for a power cut, then say \emph{pañcam} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{பஞ்சம்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A scarcity; a famine\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{துரு} (turu)}{துரு (turu)}]{\ta{துரு} (turu) — rust}

\label{lesson:TA-C445-turu-rust}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a power cut, then the Tamil for a scarcity.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{துரு}}
\textbf{\ta{துரு}} — \emph{turu} — \textquotedblleft{}rust\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{பழைய} \ta{இரும்புக்} \ta{கதவில்} \ta{துரு} \ta{பிடித்திருக்கிறது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{paḻaiya irumpuk katavil turu piṭittirukkiṟatu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The old iron gate has rusted.
\end{quote}

\ta{துரு} \ta{பிடி} is to rust.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{துரு}} (\emph{turu}) is native Dravidian (DEDR 3343), \textquotedblleft{}rust, verdigris\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{turu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paḻaiya irumpuk katavil turu piṭittirukkiṟatu.} — The old iron gate has rusted.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a power cut, then the Tamil for a scarcity, then say \emph{turu} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{சிரமம்} (ciramam)}{சிரமம் (ciramam)}]{\ta{சிரமம்} (ciramam) — difficulty; trouble}

\label{lesson:TA-C445-ciramam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a scarcity, then the Tamil for rust.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{சிரமம்}}
\textbf{\ta{சிரமம்}} — \emph{ciramam} — \textquotedblleft{}difficulty; trouble\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{மின்வெட்டால்} \ta{எல்லோருக்கும்} \ta{சிரமமாக} \ta{இருந்தது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{miṉveṭṭāl ellōrukkum ciramamāka iruntatu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The power cut made things hard for everyone.
\end{quote}

\ta{சிரமப்படு} is to struggle; \ta{சிரமம்} \ta{இல்லை}, no trouble.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{சிரமம்}} (\emph{ciramam}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{śrama}, \textquotedblleft{}labour, fatigue\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 12682).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ciramam}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ciramam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{miṉveṭṭāl ellōrukkum ciramamāka iruntatu.} — The power cut made things hard for everyone.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a scarcity, then the Tamil for rust, then say \emph{ciramam} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{சிரமம்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Difficulty; trouble\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{அதிர்} (atir)}{அதிர் (atir)}]{\ta{அதிர்} (atir) — to shake; to vibrate}

\label{lesson:TA-C445-atir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for rust, then the Tamil for difficulty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{அதிர்}}
\textbf{\ta{அதிர்}} — \emph{atir} — \textquotedblleft{}to shake; to vibrate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{லாரி} \ta{போனபோது} \ta{சன்னல்கள்} \ta{அதிர்ந்தன}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{lāri pōṉapōtu caṉṉalkaḷ atirntaṉa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
When the lorry went past, the windows rattled.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ta{அதிர்ந்தது}, \emph{atirntatu}.

Said of the ground, of windows and of loud sounds.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{அதிர்}} (\emph{atir}) is native Dravidian (DEDR 137), \textquotedblleft{}to shake, to quake, to tremble\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{atir}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{atir}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lāri pōṉapōtu caṉṉalkaḷ atirntaṉa.} — When the lorry went past, the windows rattled.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for rust, then the Tamil for difficulty, then say \emph{atir} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Sprouts and Moss to Power Cuts and Shortages}

\label{lesson:TA-R445-review-439-445}



\begin{quote}
Say the Tamil for a beetle and moss.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a beetle, moss, a sapling, to sprout, to sway
  \item pollution, the environment, dust, waste, plastic
  \item to rot, to stink, to pile up, to recycle, a living creature
  \item to protect, destruction, greenery, to surround, to swing about
  \item to break off, to shatter, a crack, a hole, to scratch
  \item to spill, to scatter, to splash, a stain, to drip
  \item a power cut, a scarcity, rust, difficulty, to shake
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A beetle? (\textbf{\ta{வண்டு}}, \emph{vaṇṭu}.) Moss? (\textbf{\ta{பாசி}}, \emph{pāci}.) A sapling? (\textbf{\ta{மரக்கன்று}}, \emph{marakkaṉṟu}.) To sprout? (\textbf{\ta{முளை}}, \emph{muḷai}.) To sway? (\textbf{\ta{அசை}}, \emph{acai}.) Pollution? (\textbf{\ta{மாசு}}, \emph{mācu}.) The environment? (\textbf{\ta{சுற்றுச்சூழல்}}, \emph{cuṟṟuccūḻal}.) Dust? (\textbf{\ta{தூசி}}, \emph{tūci}.) Waste? (\textbf{\ta{கழிவு}}, \emph{kaḻivu}.) Plastic? (\textbf{\ta{நெகிழி}}, \emph{nekiḻi}.) To rot? (\textbf{\ta{அழுகு}}, \emph{aḻuku}.) To stink? (\textbf{\ta{நாறு}}, \emph{nāṟu}.) To pile up? (\textbf{\ta{குவி}}, \emph{kuvi}.) To recycle? (\textbf{\ta{மறுசுழற்சி} \ta{செய்}}, \emph{maṟucuḻaṟci cey}.) A living creature? (\textbf{\ta{உயிரினம்}}, \emph{uyiriṉam}.) To protect? (\textbf{\ta{பாதுகா}}, \emph{pātukā}.) Destruction? (\textbf{\ta{அழிவு}}, \emph{aḻivu}.) Greenery? (\textbf{\ta{பசுமை}}, \emph{pacumai}.) To surround? (\textbf{\ta{சூழ்}}, \emph{cūḻ}.) To swing about? (\textbf{\ta{ஊசலாடு}}, \emph{ūcalāṭu}.) To break off? (\textbf{\ta{ஒடி}}, \emph{oṭi}.) To shatter? (\textbf{\ta{நொறுங்கு}}, \emph{noṟuṅku}.) A crack? (\textbf{\ta{விரிசல்}}, \emph{virical}.) A hole? (\textbf{\ta{ஓட்டை}}, \emph{ōṭṭai}.) To scratch? (\textbf{\ta{கீறு}}, \emph{kīṟu}.) To spill? (\textbf{\ta{சிந்து}}, \emph{cintu}.) To scatter? (\textbf{\ta{சிதறு}}, \emph{citaṟu}.) To splash? (\textbf{\ta{தெறி}}, \emph{teṟi}.) A stain? (\textbf{\ta{கறை}}, \emph{kaṟai}.) To drip? (\textbf{\ta{ஒழுகு}}, \emph{oḻuku}.) A power cut? (\textbf{\ta{மின்வெட்டு}}, \emph{miṉveṭṭu}.) A scarcity? (\textbf{\ta{பஞ்சம்}}, \emph{pañcam}.) Rust? (\textbf{\ta{துரு}}, \emph{turu}.) Difficulty? (\textbf{\ta{சிரமம்}}, \emph{ciramam}.) To shake? (\textbf{\ta{அதிர்}}, \emph{atir}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
